AcquiredSource.description:
What acquisition found about the source, before any LLM call.

Lets the import screen show a title, channel and description a few seconds after submit,
well before the plan arrives. Not model input and not persisted: `RawAcquisition` stays
internal, and this carries only its three display fields.

description.description: The source's own description or caption, verbatim.

title.description: Video or page title, as the source gives it.

AddIngredient.description: Add an ingredient line the recipe did not have.

created_at.description: When the user made the edit.

AddValue.description: An ingredient the cook added. `step` links it to a step (R6b); null in R6a.

amount.description: Null for a line with no amount.

step.description: The step that uses it, or null.

unit.description: The unit as shown, or null.

AmountValue.description: The new amount and unit. `unit` is null for "No unit" and always null for to-taste.

unit.description: The unit as shown, or null for no unit.

CookingGraph.description: The internal DAG of a recipe: what the LLM extracts, what the scheduler consumes.

cuisine.description: Cuisine, when the source states or implies one.

servings.description: Servings the quantities are stated for.

servings_stated.description: False when `servings` is a default (not stated, or discarded by the PC5 guard — a yield count the model mistook for a people count). Defaults True so every pre-P1-5 saved recipe (all hand-authored, all genuinely stated) reads as stated without a migration — see COOKING_GRAPH.md.

stages.description: Ordered stages; every node's `stage` must appear here.

stated_total_min.description: Total time the original recipe claimed. Sanity-checks extraction (§5.8).

yield_text.description: The source's own stated yield, e.g. "14 rasgulla". Null when not stated or not grounded by a number in the source text.

CookingPlan.description: The scheduled, renderable output the user sees.

critical_path.description: Node ids on the longest path.

graph_id.description: Id of the graph this plan was computed from.

saved_min.description: serial_min - total_min. The number the product is arguing for.

scheduled.description: Every node, placed on the timeline.

serial_min.description: Sum of all typical durations, done one at a time.

warnings.description: Safety-check findings (§4.5). "degraded" means extraction fell back.

windows.description: Wait windows derived from the timeline.

DraftStep.description: One step of a streamed draft. The text and its origin: never a duration field.

added.description: The model marked this step as one it added because the source skips it (`origin="added"`, FGC-3). The draft labels it; the validated plan decides.

text.description: The model's step text, as streamed (lightly normalized).

GraphProvenance.description:
Sibling record to a `CookingGraph`, keyed by node id.

Deliberately not a field on `Node` (design doc §5, "Where confidence/provenance
lives") — computed by `provenance.py` alongside `graph.py`'s output, so `Node` and
the golden fixtures stay byte-identical.

ImportJobResponse.description:
`GET /import/{job_id}` — the client polls this (design doc §4.5).

A separate envelope from `RecipePlanResponse`, which stays the frozen contract for
the fixture path (design doc §9 decision 3).

acquired.description: Title, channel and description once acquire has returned (not for pasted text). Kept on every later status, like `preview`.

draft.description: The ingredients and steps as the extraction call streams them, before validation. Kept on every later status, like `preview`, so a failed job still shows what was read. `None` for a result-cache hit, or when streaming is off.

preview.description: The source's own readable recipe, once acquire has produced one (A2). Kept on every later status, so a failed or degraded job can still show it.

result.description: Present once status is a terminal value (done / method_not_grounded).

status.description: Where the job is in the pipeline.

ImportMeta.description:
Import-status fields from `ImportResult` that `RecipePlanResponse` doesn't carry.

`RecipePlanResponse` stays the frozen `{graph, plan, stages}` contract (M2.9 decision
3); this is a sibling field so a saved-and-reopened recipe can still show that its
plan was simplified or its timings estimated (A6) instead of looking like a normal
plan. `degraded` is computed once by the client at save time from
`"degraded" in warnings` -- not a new server field.

ImportOriginal.description:
Everything post-processing reads, kept so a saved recipe can be re-processed free.

`extract/postprocess.py::reprocess` rebuilds the graph and plan from this alone:
no acquire, no LLM. Immutable after save (staleness plan B1, B5). `recipe` is the
extraction model's own output, *before* title resolution and *before* any repair --
both of those are post-processing and are re-derived on every refresh.

graph_id.description: Kept so a session's graph id is stable across a refresh.

repair.description: The repair proposal the cold import applied, replayed without a call.

ImportResult.description:
The `/import` response payload.

A separate envelope from `RecipePlanResponse` (design doc §9 decision 3) — that
response stays the frozen contract for the fixture path.

failure.description: Set only with `status == 'failed'`: whether the provider was unavailable or the extraction came back incomplete. Failed results are never cached or saved.

ingredients.description: Present even at Tier 0 — a shopping list is real recovered information.

original.description: The post-processing inputs, set on `done` so the client can keep them with a saved recipe and refresh it without an LLM call (staleness plan B1).

postprocess_version.description: `POSTPROCESS_VERSION` of the code that produced this result. Set on `done`.

sources.description: Which RawAcquisition legs were non-empty for this import (M2.10). Set on both Tier 0 and `done` results — a Tier 0 screen can say 'no captions on this video' without another round trip.

Ingredient.description:
One ingredient line from the source recipe.

A `prep_note` is a hint that a prep node exists: "2 onions, finely chopped"
implies a `chop_onion` node even when no written step mentions chopping.

group.description: Ingredient grouping, e.g. "For the masala" / "For garnish".

optional.description: Optional ingredients are exempt from the consumption invariant (§5.5).

prep_note.description: Preparation stated on the ingredient line, e.g. "finely chopped".

qty.description: Quantity, or null when the recipe gives none.

qty_amount.description: Structured form of `qty_text`, set only when it parsed with certainty. Null means the amount cannot be scaled (vague, a second amount, a package size, ...) and is shown as written.

qty_text.description: Quantity as the source stated it, e.g. "1 1/4", "2-3", "a pinch". Display fallback when `qty` cannot be parsed as a single number, and the honest form of ranges and vague amounts that `qty` would otherwise lose.

unit_canonical.description: `unit` mapped to one canonical spelling (g, kg, ml, l, tsp, tbsp, cup, katori, glass, oz, lb, pinch, count), or null when the unit is absent or not in the closed alias table. Never guessed; `unit` itself is not rewritten.

IngredientAnchor.description: Where an ingredient edit applies: a position in `graph.ingredients` plus its guard.

IngredientExpected.description: What the ingredient line looked like when the edit was made (its anchor's guard).

LongWait.description:
An idle stretch long enough to leave the kitchen.

Not long enough to be a separate sitting (`LONG_WAIT_MIN` <= idle < `SESSION_BREAK_MIN`).

host_node_ids.description: Hands-off nodes running during the stretch, in scheduled order. Often more than one consecutive unattended node with no single host.

Node.description:
One unit of work in the cooking graph.

`kind` and `attention` are separate on purpose. `attention` decides whether the
node occupies the cook and therefore whether it creates a wait window; `kind`
decides how it renders. Scheduler code must branch on `attention` only.

attention.description: Whether the cook is occupied. `unattended` and `periodic` create windows.

consumes.description: Ingredient ids and/or component ids this node uses up.

depends_on.description: Node ids that must COMPLETE before this node may start.

doneness_cue.description: Sensory finish signal, e.g. "onions light golden, oil separating".

duration_max.description: Pessimistic duration; window-safety checks use this.

duration_typical.description: Duration the plan displays and schedules on.

instruction.description: Full sentence(s) shown in step mode.

interruptible.description: Whether the cook can drop this mid-way and return. Gates `periodic` windows.

kind.description: Render classification. Not used by the scheduler.

label.description: UI heading, four words or fewer.

max_lead_min.description: Freshness ceiling: minutes this may finish before its consumer starts (§4.5).

produces.description: Component id this node yields, e.g. "comp_base".

stage.description: Id of the stage this node belongs to; must exist in `stages`.

station.description: The resource this node contends for.

tip.description: Optional aside shown in step mode.

NodeProvenance.description: Per-node provenance: how each field's value was arrived at, plus freshness.

origin.description: added when ABC Cook added this step because the source skips it (FGC-3); source otherwise, including for a provenance record saved before this field existed.

NormalizedChapter.description:
A YouTube chapter marker. Grounded, but stage-level — never a node duration.

See design doc §0: a chapter delta measures how long the creator spent on screen,
not how long the cook will spend. Used only by `corroborate.py`.

end_sec.description: Chapter end, in seconds. Null for the last chapter if unknown.

start_sec.description: Chapter start, in seconds from video start.

NormalizedIngredient.description:
One ingredient line, structured but not yet graph-ready.

`qty` stays a free-text string, not a float: real sources state quantities as
"a little less than 2", "1/2", or ranges, which cannot be honestly forced into a
single number here. `graph.py` does that best-effort conversion, not this model.

group.description: Ingredient grouping, e.g. "For tadka", when the source states one.

name.description: As named in the source. Never invented.

prep_note.description: Stated on the ingredient line itself, e.g. "finely chopped".

qty.description: Quantity as stated, verbatim or lightly normalized.

NormalizedRecipe.description:
The real, inspectable value that crosses the normalize -> graph seam.

`method_grounded` is the model's own claim and MUST NOT be trusted as-is
(§10.C finding 1): `normalize.py`'s Tier 0 gate recomputes it as `bool(steps)`
before any caller acts on it.

method_grounded.description: The model's own claim about whether method text existed. A hint only — callers must independently verify via `bool(steps)`.

notes.description: Free-text notes for a human reviewer: ambiguities, translation doubts, etc.

servings.description: How many PEOPLE this feeds — only if the source states that, in those terms. Never the yield count (how many pieces/items the recipe makes) — that goes in yield_text instead. If the source only gives a piece count ("makes 14 rasgulla") with no separate people count, leave this null; do not copy the piece count here.

stated_total_min.description: ONLY an explicit stated total-time claim. Never derived from video duration.

title.description: A clean dish name (e.g. "Buttermilk Pancakes"), NOT the raw source title verbatim -- the source's own title is preserved separately as ImportResult.source_title regardless of what you put here. Never invent a name unrelated to the source: title.py only accepts this claim when every word in it is grounded in the raw title or a linked blog's own name (case-folded, light stemming), and replaces it with a deterministic cleanup of the raw title otherwise -- so an invented word is simply discarded, not shown to the cook.

yield_text.description: The source's own stated yield, verbatim or lightly trimmed — whatever it actually says it makes ("14 rasgulla", "2 loaves", "8 people"), including a unit/item word even when that's just a count of people. Only if a number is stated; null if the source gives no number at all ("makes a dozen" has no digit — leave this null rather than converting words to a number).

NormalizedStep.description:
One candidate node, before `graph.py` decides how to build it.

Mirrors the shape of `Node` closely enough that `graph.py` is mostly a direct
translation, but stays looser where real sources are messy (`duration_*` as
`float | None` rather than required ints) and adds the hint/verification fields
§10.C's independent-verification rule needs.

attach_to_step.description: 0-based position of the required step this optional/alternative instruction belongs with. Null when role is required.

attention.description: The model's classification. MUST default to hands_on when no explicit cue is present (design doc §5) — graph.py re-checks this via attention_cue before trusting periodic/unattended.

attention_cue.description: Verbatim source phrase justifying periodic/unattended. Null when attention is hands_on. graph.py must confirm this string actually appears in the source text before honoring a non-hands_on attention.

consumes_ingredients.description: Ingredient names (matching NormalizedIngredient.name), OR a produces_component label from an earlier step, when this step uses that earlier step's output.

depends_on_previous.description: LEGACY (prompt v1/v2). Consecutive stated steps default to sequential (§4.7). False only when the model asserts genuine independence; graph.py still applies the two-condition test (no shared ingredient/component, no produces/consumes link) before honoring False. Ignored once depends_on_steps is provided.

depends_on_steps.description: 0-based positions of the EARLIER steps whose output or pan/vessel state this step directly needs. [] means it genuinely needs nothing earlier. None means not provided -- graph.py then falls back to depends_on_previous. A claim, not a fact: graph.py verifies it.

doneness_cue.description: A qualitative phrase, only if textually present, e.g. "until golden".

duration_stated.description: True only if a number was written in the source text; False if this is a plausible estimate from a vague-but-present cue ("cook until golden"). graph.py applies the §4.7 low-end clamp (duration_typical = duration_min) to window-host nodes when this is False.

freshness.description: See module docstring: never invent a number for stated_unbounded.

freshness_cue.description: Verbatim source phrase, when freshness != none. graph.py should require this to carry a genuine immediacy marker ("immediately", "just before serving") before trusting stated_unbounded — a bare "serve" is not one (§10.C finding 3).

interruptible.description: Almost never stated; §4.7 default is prep=true, active/finish=false.

label.description: A short (1-4 word) UI heading for this step -- a summary in your own words (e.g. "Mix marinade", "First rise"), not a truncation of text. Null if you have none. graph.py accepts it only by shape (word count, no leading conditional marker, no trailing preposition/conjunction) and falls back to its own trim of `text` otherwise -- it is never checked against `text` for topical match, so accuracy is still your job.

max_lead_min.description: ONLY populated for stated_numeric. Never a guessed number.

origin.description: source for every step the source describes, even when you reword it. added only for a step you add because the source skips something the dish cannot be made without (see the prompt section "Steps the source skips"); the cook is shown it as added by the app, not by the source. Never added for a source with no method of its own.

produces_component.description: Freeform label for what this step yields -- set it only when a LATER step will name this exact label in its own consumes_ingredients.

role.description: required: part of cooking the dish. optional: conditional or nice-to-have ("If you plan to...", "if desired"). alternative: another way to do an earlier step ("Microwave method: ..."). Never drop an optional/alternative instruction; mark it here instead.

role_cue.description: Verbatim source phrase showing the step is optional/alternative. Null when role is required. graph.py must find it in the source text before honoring a non-required role.

station.description: Explicit if stated; else the §4.7 verb-based default.

text.description: The step, lightly normalized. Never invented.

NumberAmount.description: An amount the cook typed: one number or a range.

high.description: The high end of a range; null for an exact amount. Always above `low`.

kind.description: Discriminator: a number or a range.

low.description: The number, or the low end of a range.

Phase.description:
A stretch of the plan where the cook has to be in the kitchen.

A new phase starts after a hands-free gap of >= `PHASE_BREAK_MIN`, where hands-free
means no `hands_on` and no `periodic` node is running. Measured on the *attended*
timeline, independently of `Session`/`LongWait` (which use the cook-occupied one).
Internal name -- UI copy is the renderer's job. Provisional threshold.

elapsed_high_min.description: The attended footprint of this phase's own `node_ids` on the slowed-pace timeline, clamped to be at least `elapsed_min`. Same construction as `Session.elapsed_high_min`.

end_min.description: End of this phase's attended footprint.

node_ids.description: Every node assigned to this phase, in scheduled order. A node belongs to the last phase that had started by its `start_min`.

preceded_by_host_node_ids.description: The hands-off nodes whose interval overlaps that gap. `[]` for the first phase.

preceded_by_wait_min.description: Length of the hands-free gap immediately before this phase. `None` for the first phase.

start_min.description: Start of this phase's attended footprint.

starts_new_session.description: True iff this phase's start is the start of a `Session` other than the first. False for the first phase.

PlanSummary.description:
Recipe-level timing, derived from the scheduled plan. See `schedule/summary.py`.

Every field here is computed, never authored — the frontend is forbidden from
deriving any of these numbers itself (`CLAUDE.md`). Optional on `RecipePlanResponse`
so a plan serialized before this field existed still round-trips.

attended_min.description: `active_min` plus Σ `duration_typical` over every `periodic` node — what being in the kitchen costs, not just what the cook's hands do.

elapsed_high_min.description: Makespan with every `hands_on` node's `duration_typical` set to its `duration_max`; hands-off nodes untouched. The honest upper bound of the range.

elapsed_min.description: Copy of `plan.total_min`, so the UI reads one object.

long_waits.description: Idle stretches >= `LONG_WAIT_MIN` that are not session breaks.

phases.description: The timeline partitioned at hands-free gaps >= `PHASE_BREAK_MIN`, measured on the attended (hands_on or periodic) timeline. `None` only for a plan serialized before this field existed; new plans always carry >= 1 phase.

sessions.description: The timeline partitioned at idle stretches >= `SESSION_BREAK_MIN`.

PreviewSection.description: A run of source lines under an optional heading, e.g. "FOR THE SYRUP".

heading.description: Section title as the source gave it.

lines.description: Source lines, verbatim apart from tag/entity cleanup.

QtyAmount.description:
A quantity parsed from the source text, structured so it can be multiplied.

Present only when the parser (`abc_cook.extract.quantity.parse_amount`) was certain; the
line then reads back as `prefix + number(s) + rest`. Everything it is not certain about
has no `QtyAmount`, and the line renders as the source wrote it.

high.description: The high end of a range (always above `low`); null for an exact amount.

low.description: The number, or the low end of a range.

prefix.description: An approximate word kept verbatim, e.g. "about ".

rest.description: The source text after the number(s), verbatim, e.g. " cup", "g", " pieces".

RecipeListResponse.description: Every recipe the API can currently serve.

RecipePlanResponse.description:
Everything the Plan view needs, in one round trip.

The graph rides along because the plan is node *ids* and timings — the labels,
instructions and ingredients the renderer draws all live on the graph. Shipping both
keeps the frontend a pure renderer: it joins by id, and computes nothing.

stages.description: Per-stage rollups, in `graph.stages` order. See schedule/rollup.py.

summary.description: Recipe-level timing. See schedule/summary.py. `None` for a plan serialized before this field existed.

RecipeSummary.description: One row in the recipe list.

id.description: Slug used in the plan URL.

servings.description: Servings the quantities are stated for.

RemoveIngredient.description: Take an ingredient line off the list.

created_at.description: When the user made the edit.

RepairProposal.description:
The repair call's entire response shape.

One `StepRepair` per original step, in the same order. Matched back to the
original steps by position — there is no id/index field because the count and
order are already fixed by the request.

ReprocessRequest.description: `POST /recipes/reprocess` body: the inputs a saved recipe kept (staleness plan B2).

ReprocessResponse.description:
`POST /recipes/reprocess` response: the refreshed derived copy.

`payload` and `import_meta` are exactly what a client stores beside `original` in a
`SavedRecipe`; `postprocess_version` is the stamp it writes with them. Computed with
no acquire and no LLM call.

SavedLibrary.description: The whole saved-recipe library, as stored under one `localStorage` key.

recipes.description: Saved entries, in no particular order.

version.description: Storage format version. The web store also reads version 1 (no `original`, `postprocess_version` or `edits`) and migrates it on first write; this model describes v2 only.

SavedRecipe.description: One recipe a user has saved on this device.

edits.description: The cook's edits (R6), as a patch over `payload`. Readers keep items they do not understand verbatim.

id.description: Stable id for this saved entry, assigned at first save.

import_meta.description: Import-status context alongside `payload` (A6). Null for fixture-path recipes, which never went through `/import`.

original.description: The post-processing inputs from the import, immutable after save. `payload` and `import_meta` are derived from it and can be rebuilt free via `POST /recipes/reprocess`. Null for a feed save or a legacy import.

postprocess_version.description: `POSTPROCESS_VERSION` of the code that produced `payload`. Null means unknown, which is treated as stale.

saved_at.description: When this entry was first saved. Never changes.

servings_choice.description: The cook's chosen servings for this recipe (R4b). Null or absent means as written. Additive in v2. The web app reconciles it against `payload` on read; nothing here checks it against the recipe.

source_key.description: Canonical key derived from the source's URL/text; see module docstring.

updated_at.description: When this entry's payload was last replaced. Equals saved_at on first save.

ScheduledNode.description: One node placed on the timeline.

end_min.description: Minutes from the start of cooking.

node_id.description: Id of the node in the source graph.

occupies_cook.description: Whether the cook is busy for this interval. Follows `Node.attention`.

rank_in_window.description: Order within the window. 0 is the task the UI promotes as "start with this".

start_min.description: Minutes from the start of cooking.

window_id.description: Set when this ran inside another node's wait window.

ServerInfo.description: `GET /health`: liveness plus the version stamp saved recipes are compared against.

postprocess_version.description: `POSTPROCESS_VERSION`: a saved recipe stamped lower may be out of date.

ServingsByBatch.description: The recipe does not state its servings, so the cook picked a relative size (R4).

ServingsByCount.description: The recipe states how many it serves, so the cook picked a headcount (R4).

original.description: The servings the recipe stated when this was chosen; a mismatch voids it.

Session.description:
A contiguous sitting: cooking activity uninterrupted by a session-break wait.

Internal name — never shown to the user (`CLAUDE.md` § Vocabulary). The Plan and
Cooking Mode talk about the *situation* ("start about 24 hr before you eat"), never
the model.

elapsed_high_min.description: The occupied footprint of this sitting's own `node_ids`, measured on a timeline where every `hands_on` node's `duration_typical` is set to its `duration_max`. The header range's upper bound for the last sitting. Not derivable from `PlanSummary.elapsed_high_min - start_min`: slowness in earlier sittings shifts later ones on that timeline, but this sitting's own steps still take the same honest-worst-case time regardless of what came before.

elapsed_min.description: `end_min - start_min`. How long this sitting takes at typical pace. For the last sitting, the header range's lower bound; for a single-sitting recipe, equal to `plan.total_min`.

end_min.description: End of this sitting's hands-on footprint.

node_ids.description: Every node assigned to this sitting, in scheduled order.

preceded_by_host_node_ids.description: The hands-off nodes whose interval overlaps the open gap between the previous sitting's end and this sitting's start -- what the dish is busy with during the break. `[]` for the first sitting. Same predicate as `LongWait.host_node_ids`.

preceded_by_wait_min.description: Length of the session-break gap immediately before this sitting. `None` for the first sitting.

start_min.description: Start of this sitting's hands-on footprint.

SetIngredientAmount.description: Change an ingredient line's amount and unit.

created_at.description: When the user made the edit.
When the user made the edit.

SetStepText.description: Rewrite a step's text. The plan's timing is not recomputed (R6b).

created_at.description: When the user made the edit.

SourcePreview.description:
The source's own recipe text, readable before any LLM call (A2).

Deliberately a third layer, separate from `NormalizedRecipe` (LLM output) and
`CookingGraph`/`CookingPlan` (validated, scheduled): it holds *strings only* --
no parsed quantities, no durations, no computed numbers -- so nothing downstream
can mistake it for validated data, and rendering it never needs the scheduler.

ingredients.description: Ingredient lines verbatim, e.g. "200 g flour (7 oz)".

instructions.description: Method, in source order; one headingless section when the source has none.

title.description: The page's recipe name, as published.

value.description: The URL, the image reference, or the pasted text itself.

Stage.description:
A named group of nodes: Prep, Cook Base, Add Veggies, Finish.

Stages are user-facing and ordered; the Plan view groups by them.

color_key.description: Key into the stage palette in docs/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md.

StageSpan.description:
A stage's footprint on the scheduled timeline.

Deliberately NOT part of `CookingPlan`: it is a view over a finished plan, computed
by `abc_cook.schedule.rollup`, and adding it to the plan would rewrite all five
golden fixtures for a rendering convenience.

It exists because the Plan view shows a per-stage minute count, and the frontend is
forbidden from deriving one (CLAUDE.md). Stages interleave — in Kadai Paneer `prep`
spans 0-19 while `cook_base` spans 3-22 — so a stage is a span, not a block.

elapsed_min.description: Wall-clock span of the stage. Overlaps other stages' spans.

end_min.description: Latest end among this stage's nodes.

hands_on_min.description: Of `inline_work_min`, minutes on nodes with `attention == "hands_on"`. `hands_on_min + unattended_min == inline_work_min`. Optional for backward compatibility with plans serialized before this field existed.

inline_work_min.description: `work_min - windowed_work_min`. What the stage's own card still shows.

node_ids.description: This stage's nodes, in scheduled order.

stage_id.description: Id of the stage in the source graph.

start_min.description: Earliest start among this stage's nodes.

unattended_min.description: Of `inline_work_min`, minutes on nodes with `attention in ("unattended", "periodic")` — the nodes that do not continuously occupy the cook (§4) and are the only ones that can host a window (§4.3). Includes `periodic`, despite the name: "not hands-on" is the scheduler's own binary. `work_min == hands_on_min + unattended_min + windowed_work_min`, since windowed work is always hands-on (`scheduler.py` only claims `hands_on` nodes into a window). Optional for backward compatibility with plans serialized before this field existed.

windowed_work_min.description: Of `work_min`, the minutes absorbed into another stage's wait window.

work_min.description: Sum of `duration_typical` over the stage's nodes.

StepAnchor.description: Where a step edit applies: the expected text, with the index as a tiebreak.

StepExpected.description: What the step read when the edit was made.

StepRepair.description:
The only three fields a repair pass may ever set, for one step.

Every field defaults to None, meaning "leave the extracted value unchanged" (CP2
decision D). A default of True/[] used to *overwrite* extraction: a response that
simply omitted `depends_on_previous` reset an extracted, verified independence
claim to sequential. See `_merge_repair` for how each field is applied -- repair
fixes structure additively; it never resets a semantic decision to a default.

consumes_ingredients.description: Names to ADD to this step's consumes. Omit to leave unchanged.

depends_on_previous.description: true to make this step wait for the previous one. Omit to leave unchanged. Repair can add a dependency; it can never remove one.

produces_component.description: Set only to name a component a later step uses. Omit to leave unchanged.

StreamedDraft.description:
What the extraction call has said so far, before anything is validated.

Unvalidated and labelled a draft on screen. It carries no durations, timers, offsets,
totals or servings, by construction: the scanner that fills it reads nothing but the
ingredient lines and each step's text. The validated plan replaces it, one tap away.

calls.description: Extraction calls started so far (a retry or escalation shows as 2). A later call only fills a section still empty; it never rewrites what is shown.

ingredients.description: Each ingredient once its line has closed, in the order the model wrote them. Append-only.

ingredients_complete.description: The model has finished the ingredients list (`[]` plus this is an empty list).
